title: Migration identity and Audit installation chain
question: How does Audit take ownership of audit_log without breaking 0.7.0 installations, published migrations or named storages?

options.text: Published fixed-basename adoption migration (chosen): No table for core-only installs; zero row rewrite.
Auto-loaded audit migration: Creates the table for every install.
Keep audit_log in core schema: Contradicts module ownership.

context: Independent architecture review (revision 2) requested by the owner (brief M6, M7). Phase tasks and implementation remain deferred. Refines D3 without contradicting it.
decision: The two shipped core migration basenames never change and stay published with plain publishes(); after the split StorageSchema::create/drop handle six tables. Audit ships one migration with a new fixed later basename, published (not auto-loaded) under its own tag with plain publishes(); up() creates or adopts after a full shape check, down() never drops data. Audit adds azguard:audit:migration {storage} for named storages. StorageMigrated/StorageHealth verify six core tables; Audit contributes table presence and shape checks. Journal pruning uses its own short transactions without the authority lock.
rationale: Laravel keys migrations by basename and publishesMigrations() re-dates files, so identities must be fixed; 0.7.0 named-storage migrations created audit_log through core; the current doctor requires audit_log for every storage. Publishing on demand keeps core-only installs free of the audit table.
consequences: Fresh audited installs need one publish step; doctor names it.
Published copies of core migrations change effective behavior; documented.

evidence.note: Owner requested an independent review and authorized amending Codex decisions within the owner principles.
